questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I went to Svalbard due to the unique nature and geology. The courses sounded exciting - and it has lived up to my expectations! I Wanted to go to the arctic and learn more about this, since I'm interested in climate and the poles are really affected by changing climate - and Svalbard must be one of the best places to learn about this!

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy, but I was very happy that we were serval students arriving the same day, so we could figure things out together!

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: In the reception in UNIS the receptionist gave us a lot of information. Also, we had a 3 days "course" were information about courses, UNIS and living in Svalbard and studying in the arctic were given.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy. UNIS sends a link to Samskipnaden Studenthousing (Elvesletta, Longyearbyen) when you accept the spot for the courses. This is the only option for exchange students - but it is a really nice place to live with good facilities.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Living in the studenthousing is great! Be open and try to do things with your kitchen friends:))

Additional comments:

questions.answer: I went to the receptionist and she helped me. It was super easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The receptionist at UNIS

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into the courses I applied for...

questions.answer: Apply for courses that you have the background for

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think the level was good. In one of the courses I took I had heard of many of the processes before, since I had a course covering approximately the same in my program in Copenhagen. But it was more focusing on Svalbard and that was very interesting. I came to Svalbard because I wanted to do a lot o field work and I have learned a lot about that!! There is a lot of written reports and bigger projects and much work is done independently - and I have learned a lot from this, since I had no real experience in writing before!

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In Copenhagen we get a lot of help always and we have lectures and exercises every week (so a lecture about something and then an exercise about the same thing). In UNIS this is different because you need to do field work when the sun is still up! Therefore we had a lot of lectures in the first course where almost all knowledge were told - then we did field work and wrote reports, and had only a few lectures after the field work. In the course that started later we had topics like in copenhagen and often an exercise in the end of the week, but also here the written part were a bigger part than at home. Also, the field work in this course were the end of many lectures, and after this there were 1 month of writing report and working independently in the lab.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
AG-210: The Quarternary and Glacial Geology of Svalbard (15 ECTS)
AG-211: Arctic Marine Geology (15 ECTS)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend these courses for geology! But I know they will be changed in 2-3 years...

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: UNIS don't have so much non-academic - but the opportunities in Longyearbyen is very good!!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
Nothing from UNIS.
But there is a gym, swimming pool, football and hockey... And it does not cost that much and there is often student rabat.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Be part of the gym and/or the sport activities!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go for hikes!! Must go to the student cabin and I will also recommend Nordenskiold cabin. Visit Longyearbreen and/or Larsbreen and the ice caves when its cold! Visit Pyramiden!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Longyearbyen is a strange place with only 2600 people - many are norwegian, but in general there is a very international community here! But take part in local events is nice! (Ps. you need facebook to go to Svalbard since they have a group for everything fx Northern lights in Longyearbyen, Sysselmesteren, info in Longyearbyen... etc)

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: There is no local students. Everyone is exchange students and  I think that is really nice since every one want to get new friends!

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I have met many different cultures and it is fun to learn from so many different people!

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The international culture :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open to meet new people!
Go on a lot of hikes!
Don't be afraid to try something new!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: We are in the arctic and there is a lot of outdoor activity and you can get cold - don't be scared of being cold and dirty - but enjoy your stay!!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I have no idea... I have developed my social skills and my english and learned a lot in geology and learned to be much more independent in my work! I have hiked a lot and just enjoyed being here...

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Writing the bigger project, doing research on my own and working in the lab and get to understand the samples and the processes!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
